title: Not Bacteria After All
question: Are archaea just odd bacteria?
hook: For decades, microbes that looked like bacteria were filed as bacteria, until their genes said otherwise.
idea: Archaea are a separate domain of life, found almost everywhere and not only in extreme places.

beats.prompt: In 1977 Carl Woese and George Fox compare the ribosomal RNA genes of microbes then filed as bacteria. What do they conclude?

choices.label: They are bacteria with an unusual metabolism
choices.feedback: That was how they were filed before, but the gene evidence pointed elsewhere.

choices.label: They are a separate line of descent from bacteria
They are eukaryotes
choices.feedback: Archaea have some genes closer to eukaryotes, but Woese and Fox found a separate line, not eukaryotes.

beats.explain: Woese and Fox gave the first evidence for Archaebacteria as a separate line of descent, from ribosomal RNA genes, missing peptidoglycan and unusual coenzymes.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in archaea history in order
items: Methane-producing species are first grown in pure culture, classed as bacteria (1930s and 1940s)
Zuckerkandl and Pauling propose using gene sequences to relate prokaryotes (1965)
Woese and Fox classify archaea separately from bacteria (1977)
beats.explain: The sentences date these steps to the 1930s and 1940s, 1965, 1977 and 2003.

beats.prompt: Sort each habitat by when archaea were found there
groups: Where the first ones were seen
items: Where the first ones were seen
Where the first ones were seen
beats.explain: The first observed archaea lived in hot springs and salt lakes; improved detection tools later found them in almost every habitat, including soil, oceans and marshlands.

beats.prompt: Match each archaeon or group to its feature
pairs: Make methane and help digestion in humans and ruminants
Use sunlight as an energy source
beats.explain: Each pairing shows the diversity of archaea in energy, shape and structure.
